evals.name: data-model-split-origin-layer-severity-table
evals.prompt: I'm about to change the Member data model: replace `fullName` with `givenName` and `familyName`, and add an optional `phoneNumber`. Before I touch anything, work out what else this change affects across the docs, API spec, UI code and tests in this repo. Write impact.md with a per-artifact assessment and a recommendation on whether I can go ahead. Do not edit any existing file. This runs unattended: do not ask questions, state assumptions in impact.md.
evals.expected_output: All three named with the reason each breaks; Threat model PII gap and AC-3.2 both found; Origin layer, full per-artifact table with all three statuses, recommendation tied to the BREAKING count; Stops on BREAKING, concrete order of updates; Statuses defensible for every row
expectations: [r1] Finds the breaking consumers: openapi.yaml Member requires fullName, ProfileCard.tsx reads u.fullName, contract test pins ['email','fullName','id']: All three named with the reason each breaks

[r2] Finds the non-code ripple: threat model must classify phoneNumber (new PII) and fullName's classification no longer maps; requirements AC-3.2 says 'full name'; test strategy needs updating: Threat model PII gap and AC-3.2 both found

[r3] Follows the skill's procedure: states the origin layer (data model), uses the BREAKING/STALE/UNAFFECTED scale per artifact including UNAFFECTED ones (NFRs), and ends with the matching recommendation type: Origin layer, full per-artifact table with all three statuses, recommendation tied to the BREAKING count

[r4] Recommendation surfaces the BREAKING impacts before proceeding and says who/what must be updated first (API contract and consumers, threat model data classification), rather than 'go ahead and update as you go': Stops on BREAKING, concrete order of updates
[r5] Does not overstate: NFRs and HLD not marked BREAKING without a reason; no invented artifacts: Statuses defensible for every row

evals.name: lambda-cache-conditional-go-stale-only
evals.prompt: To cut DynamoDB reads I'm going to add a 5-minute in-memory cache inside the Profile Lambda for GET /members/{id}, keyed by id. It's purely an implementation detail: no API, schema or UI change. Check whether that's true against the design artifacts in this repo before I start, and write impact-cache.md with your assessment and a go/no-go recommendation. Do not edit any existing file. Do not ask questions; state assumptions instead.
evals.expected_output: Risk named with the T1 link and the condition (check ownership before serving from cache); Found with the PATCH/US-4 link and a fix (invalidate on write or skip cache for owner after write); Origin layer and per-artifact statuses match this pattern with reasons; Conditional go with the two conditions and follow-up doc/test updates
expectations: [r1] Finds the authorization ordering risk: a cache keyed only by id, if read before the owner check, returns another member's email, defeating T1: Risk named with the T1 link and the condition (check ownership before serving from cache)

[r2] Finds the staleness problem: PATCH /members/{id} (US-4 edit display name) leaves a stale cached profile for up to 5 minutes unless invalidated: Found with the PATCH/US-4 link and a fix (invalidate on write or skip cache for owner after write)

[r3] Classifies artifacts on the skill's scale with origin layer = implementation: API, data model, UX UNAFFECTED; threat model, HLD and test strategy STALE; recommendation of the STALE-only or CONTAINED type with conditions: Origin layer and per-artifact statuses match this pattern with reasons
[r4] Proportionate: does not call the change BREAKING or block it outright; gives a conditional go: Conditional go with the two conditions and follow-up doc/test updates
